quests.conceptTitle: Modifier Placement: Focus/Scope Adverb Placement - Avoiding Misplacement
quests.targetSentence: The coupon applies only to online purchases, not in-store ones.
quests.awkwardSentence: Only the coupon applies to online purchases not instore ones.
quests.ruleExplanation: Placing 'only' before 'applies' would wrongly suggest nothing else about the coupon is true. It belongs directly before 'to online purchases', the exact thing being limited.
quests.nativeTip: A common mistake is placing this word right before the main verb - instead, place it directly before the specific thing it's limiting.
quests.visualAnchor: 🎯 Place 'only' right next to the word it describes: 'The coupon applies only to online purchases, not in-store ones.'
quests.comedyNote: Misplacing 'only' produces awkward phrasing like: 'Only the coupon applies to online purchases not instore ones.'. Always anchor modifiers adjacent to the words they modify.

quests.nativeTip: A common mistake is placing this word right before the verb, which would suggest they finished nothing - instead, place it before the quantity word it limits.
quests.visualAnchor: 🎯 Place 'almost' right next to the word it describes: 'The team finished almost every task before the deadline.'
quests.comedyNote: Misplacing 'almost' produces awkward phrasing like: 'Almost the team finished every task before the deadline.'. Always anchor modifiers adjacent to the words they modify.
